summary: Three TurboQuant+ experiment branches read from a local clone. CONFIRMED: experiment/context-scaling-fix and experiment/speed-optimization are the same commit, 367bb2dbbb562c9e78c162f3c9bea2c584482159 (2026-03-25 20:25 -0500); both are ancestors of current main@ba52ad1, which is 302 commits ahead. experiment/decode-speed-parity@2461b261 forks from 367bb2d and adds 3 docs. All three are DOCS-ONLY vs their fork points: context-scaling-fix's 15 unique commits touch README.md, 7 new docs, scripts/turbo-quality-gate.sh and .github/workflows/ci.yml only; decode-speed-parity adds docs/experiment-decode-speed.md, docs/experiment-decode-fp16-lut-results.md, docs/turboquant-plus-experiments.md. The KV-cache code is NOT here - it lives in the separate fork TheTom/llama-cpp-turboquant. So 'what it changes vs main' = documentation, a PPL+context-scaling CI gate, and recorded measurements, not code. context-scaling-fix/speed-optimization: a prefill-speed campaign on Apple M5 Max 128GB, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, flash-attn ON. Journey 739->1074->1411->1424->2095->2747 tok/s vs q8_0 2694; final block-32 + graph-side WHT = 1.02x q8_0, PPL 5.460 vs 5.414 (32-chunk), 4.6x compression. Context scaling after the optimized-dequant fix is flat 0.987-0.995x from 2K to 32K (before: 0.976/0.960/0.921x at 1K/2K/4K). Failed: group-32 rotation (PPL 7.06), custom GGML_OP_TURBO_WHT (no gain), first pre-rotate-queries attempt (PPL 23.5, a ggml column-major orientation bug, not RoPE non-commutativity). decode-speed-parity: decode is 0.84x q8_0 at 8K (65.4 vs 78.3). A no-LUT ceiling test hits 78.1 = 1.00x, proving the entire 16% gap is the 8-entry centroid constant-memory LUT (82M data-dependent accesses per decode token), and the gap widens with depth (0.88x @12 tok -> 0.76x @8K -> 0.72x @48K). 11 experiments; 2 merged (fp16 LUT, float-norm broadcast; best short 78.7, 8K 68.8, 48K 39.9); 9 dead. 'Decode-speed parity' means parity WITH q8_0 decode tok/s - not fp16, and not prefill (prefill already at 0.99-1.02x). All measurements are Apple Metal; as of the branch README CUDA was 'not yet tested'. Current main's community data: RTX 3090 CUDA, Qwen3.5-9B Q4_K_M (the target box's model) = turbo3 98.68 decode / 3707 prefill vs q8_0 102.69/3774 (0.96x/0.98x), PPL +1.3%; an older third-party CUDA port on dual 4090 is the floor at 0.385x decode.

MEASURED (docs/context-scaling-deep-dive.md): the pre-fix regression was 1024: 4796/4914=0.976x; 2048: 3036/3162=0.960x; 4096: 2371/2573=0.921x - a ~2% gap per context doubling.

MEASURED (docs/speed-experiments.md + README.md): prefill journey 739 (fp32 WHT) -> 1074 (fp16 WHT) -> 1411 (half4 butterfly) -> 1424 (pre-packed signs) -> 2095 (graph-side WHT) -> 2747 tok/s (block-32); q8_0 baseline 2694 tok/s. Final = 1.02x q8_0, PPL 5.460 vs q8_0 5.414 (32-chunk wikitext-2), 4.6x compression.

MEASURED (README.md, branch): README lists '+ optimized dequant' as 2524 tok/s = 0.98x at 4K; the doc narrative credits either optimized dequant (block-128, flat 0.98x) or block-32+graph WHT (2747, 1.02x). Both are recorded on the same branch tip and are not reconciled in-tree.

MEASURED (docs/experiment-decode-speed.md, M5 Max, 8K context): turbo3 decode 65.4 tok/s vs q8_0 78.3 = 0.84x. No-LUT ceiling (constant centroid) = 78.1 tok/s = 1.00x. Conclusion: the entire 16% decode gap is the centroid table lookup (82M constant-memory accesses per decode token at 8K, 10 attn layers, 256-dim heads).

MEASURED (docs/experiment-decode-speed.md): decode ratio degrades with depth: ~12 tok 75.3/85.2=0.88x; ~8K 59.2/77.7=0.76x; extrapolated 40K+ ~0.6x. Bit-extraction without LUT at 8K = 70.1 tok/s, so the LUT alone costs 18.5% at 8K.

MEASURED (docs/experiment-decode-fp16-lut-results.md, M5 Max): fp16 LUT (vec only) short 77.2, 8K 67.3, 48K 39.0; best variant A (half LUT + float-norm broadcast) short 78.7, 8K 68.8, 48K 39.9 tok/s; q8_0 85.2/77.7/55.6 -> variant A = 0.92x/0.89x/0.72x. PPL 6.211 (8-chunk) / 5.471 (32-chunk) unchanged.
MEASURED (commit 2461b26 message): authoritative final decode = 0.92x short, 0.88x 8K, 0.72x 48K vs q8_0; 11 experiments total, 2 merged to main, 9 dead ends.

MEASURED (docs/experiment-decode-fp16-lut-results.md): 9 dead decode experiments - register float4 select -4%, inline switch -13%, split lo/hi select -10%, precomputed centroid*norm +2%, fp16 LUT both paths -10%, custom GGML_OP_TURBO_WHT -7%, cn[] precomputed registers -10.5% (register spill), packed uint4 -5.5%, fused FA +0.9% (marginal).

MEASURED (docs/turbo-speed-investigation.md, M5 Max): the '#include "turbo-wht.h"' in ggml-metal.metal caused a SILENT CPU fallback; every benchmark before the fix measured CPU (2.4 tok/s, fake 35x regression). After inlining: MoE 10.7 tok/s gen. Real Metal numbers then 10.7 -> 51.4 (pre-rotate-queries) -> 62.2 (drop QJL) -> 77.7 (block-32), q8_0 85.5, i.e. 0.91x decode.

MEASURED (docs/turbo-speed-investigation.md): block-size diagnostic - q8_0(32) 84.1, q4_0(32) 84.2, q4_1(32) 84.6, q5_0(32) 80.6, turbo3(128) 62.5 (0.74x), turbo4(128) 42.8 (0.51x). The 26% turbo3 gap was entirely block size 128, not the centroid math.

MEASURED (docs/turbo-speed-investigation.md, external): unixsysdev pure-polar CUDA on dual 4090 shows only -0.8% speed loss at block-32; main's docs/hardware-comparison-matrix.md measures that third-party port at 0.622x prefill / 0.385x decode (missing graph-side WHT, block-32, fp16 LUT).

MEASURED (branch README.md lines 128-129): as of 2026-03-25 CUDA build was 'not yet tested' and kernels were Metal-only; current main README lists TheTom/llama-cpp-turboquant as Metal/CUDA/HIP/CPU production with prebuilt Windows CUDA binaries.

MEASURED (main docs/benchmarks.md, RTX 3090 CUDA, signalnine fork PR #24, Qwen3.5-9B Q4_K_M - the target box's model): q8_0 decode 102.69 / prefill 3774; turbo3 98.68 / 3707 (0.96x / 0.98x), PPL 8.3124 vs 8.2018 (+1.3%); turbo4 95.87 / 3628 (+1.2%); turbo2 98.05 / 3680 (+5.6%). CUDA decode within 4-7% of q8_0 across configs.

MEASURED (main docs/benchmarks.md): Sparse V dequant skips V dequant for softmax weights <1e-6; +22.8% decode at 32K, lifting turbo3 from 0.76x to 0.93x q8_0; also +5% on q8_0 itself (not compression-specific). Current main MoE decode: turbo4 79.87 (0.93x), turbo3 76.84 (0.90x) vs q8_0 85.71 short.

MEASURED (main docs/benchmarks.md): asymmetric q8_0-K + turbo4-V is the recommended pre-M5/low-tier config; M1 Max 64GB 38K: turbo4 decode 16.6 vs q8_0 12.4 (+33.9%), turbo3 7.7 (-37.9%, L2/constant-cache wall); asymmetric pp512 894.9 t/s (+2.2%) / tg128 38.64 (-2.3%).

MEASURED (main docs/benchmarks.md, AMD RX 9070 XT): symmetric turbo3 on Qwen2.5-7B Q4_K_M is catastrophic (PPL 81277) and q8_0+turbo3 NaN on HIP; q8_0-K + turbo4-V is safe (+1.0% PPL). Q4_K_M weight models must NOT use symmetric turbo.

MEASURED (docs/pre-rotate-queries-investigation.md): first pre-rotate-queries attempt gave PPL 23.5 vs baseline 6.194; the root cause was ggml column-major storage orientation of the rotation matrix, not WHT/RoPE non-commutativity (the Gemini explanation was disproven). Verified: ggml_mul_mat(A,x) with row-major-stored A computes A@x.

ESTIMATE (extrapolated from the branch docs; no 2070 SUPER measurement exists in any branch or main): the RTX 2070 SUPER (Turing sm_75, 8 GB) decode ratio for turbo3 is unknown; the nearest measured same-model CUDA point is RTX 3090 (Ampere) at 0.96x. Turing's constant-memory/cache behavior is not characterised here.
reusable_assets: scripts/turbo-quality-gate.sh (branch experiment/context-scaling-fix, commit eed5a63): two-test pre-push gate - turbo3 PPL within 5% of hardcoded q8_0 6.111, and 4K turbo3/q8_0 prefill ratio > 0.95, exit 1 on fail. Directly portable to the RTX box (env-overridable LLAMA/MODEL/WIKI vars).

Architecture recipe for fast 3-bit KV: block-size 32 + graph-side WHT rotation (Q rotate after RoPE in build_attn, V un-rotate after build_attn_mha) + pre-rotate-queries + MSE-only (drop QJL). Code lives in TheTom/llama-cpp-turboquant; the recipe and measured deltas are in docs/speed-experiments.md and docs/turbo-speed-investigation.md.

Best decode dequant variant: `constant half turbo_centroids_3bit_h[8]` (vec path only) + float4 broadcast norm multiply - docs/experiment-decode-fp16-lut-results.md 'Variant A'. +8.7% at 48K, PPL unchanged.

Sparse V dequant (main docs/benchmarks.md + docs/papers/sparse-v-dequant.md): skip V dequant where softmax weight < 1e-6; +22.8% decode at 32K and works on plain q8_0 (+5%). Minimal kernel change; the single biggest decode lever found.

Layer-adaptive / Boundary V (main docs/benchmarks.md): q8_0-V on first 2 + last 2 layers, turbo2-V elsewhere; recovers 37-91% of turbo2's quality loss at ~no speed cost. 15 lines; default-on in current fork.
Asymmetric K/V default for Q4_K_M weights: `-ctk q8_0 -ctv turbo4` (main docs/benchmarks.md); avoids the symmetric-turbo catastrophic-PPL failure on low-bit weight models.

Measurement methodology worth reusing verbatim: (a) no-op/ceiling dequant test to isolate the hot function (found the LUT is 100% of the decode gap); (b) block-size diagnostic table q8_0/q4_0/q4_1/q5_0/turbo3(128)/turbo4(128); (c) always report PPL alongside speed.

Python reference implementation: turboquant/kv_cache.py (KVCacheCompressor, memory_stats), turboquant/turboquant.py (TurboQuant with QJL, TurboQuantMSE), turboquant/polar_quant.py, qjl.py - on the branch tip. 141 pytest tests, 95% coverage gate in .github/workflows/ci.yml.
docs/hardware-comparison-matrix.md (main): decode-ratio-vs-depth table across M5 Max / M1 Max / M1 Ultra / dual-4090 CUDA - a ready template for adding an RTX 2070 SUPER row.
failures_and_lessons: `#include` inside ggml-metal.metal silently falls back to CPU; all early 'Metal' benchmarks (2.4 tok/s, fake 35x regression) measured CPU. Rule recorded in docs/turbo-speed-investigation.md: NEVER #include in ggml-metal.metal, always inline; verify the Metal library loaded before trusting any number.

Rotation group 128->32 for the quantizer (group-32 WHT) failed: PPL 7.06 vs target 6.19. Real Qwen3.5 KV tensors need 128-element groups for proper Gaussianization even though synthetic random data looked fine at d=32. Synthetic kurtosis is not a substitute for real KV tensors.

Custom GGML_OP_TURBO_WHT (O(d log d) butterfly) gave no context-scaling gain and was a net negative for decode (-6.5% to -7%) because extra graph-node/kernel-dispatch overhead dominates single-token generation. The rotation matmul was never the bottleneck.

Precomputing centroid values into an 8-float local `cn[]` array in the Metal shader caused cross-function register spill in flash attention: -10.5% decode even though only the non-vec function changed. Do not add local float arrays to FA shaders.

All 9 alternative centroid-LUT schemes (register float4 select, inline switch, split lo/hi, fp16 both paths, packed uint4) were worse or marginal; the 8-entry constant table is optimal for the current block format. Closing the decode gap needs a different block format or a custom fused-attention kernel.
Storing centroid fp16 values directly (no LUT) trades compression from 4.6x down to ~2.0x - i.e. q8_0-equivalent - defeating the purpose.

The first pre-rotate-queries attempt was misdiagnosed as WHT/RoPE non-commutativity; the real bug was ggml's column-major matrix orientation. Lesson: verify tensor-storage semantics with a 2x2 test before theorising about math.
MoE-aware expert gating for KV precision is dead: expert routing is an FFN signal, while K/V are computed in shared attention before routing, so K/V are identical regardless of experts.

The decode-speed-parity branch contains self-contradictory conclusions (an early doc says the fp16 LUT is 'net negative', later docs say it is a win and gets merged). Trust the terminal commit (2461b26) and main's current docs, not mid-branch notes.

Symmetric turbo on Q4_K_M weight models is catastrophic (PPL 3556 on Qwen2.5-7B, 81277 on AMD RX 9070 XT); K precision dominates quality. For the target box's Qwen3.5-9B Q4_K_M, use asymmetric q8_0-K + turbo-V.

Every speed number in this slice is Apple Metal (M5 Max / M1 Max); CUDA is only a third-party data point (RTX 3090: 0.96x decode, +1.3% PPL) and an older dual-4090 floor (0.385x decode). Nothing here is measured on Turing/sm_75.

hypothesis_seeds.claim: On the RTX 2070 SUPER (Turing sm_75, 8 GB) with Qwen3.5-9B Q4_K_M, turbo3 KV cache reaches >=0.90x of q8_0 decode and >=0.95x prefill at 4K-8K, i.e. the centroid-LUT penalty that costs 12-16% on Apple Metal is smaller on CUDA constant memory.
hypothesis_seeds.falsifier: Build the CUDA fork on the 2070S and measure llama-bench -ctk turbo3 -ctv turbo3 vs q8_0 at pp512/tg128 and pp8192/tg128; claim is false if turbo3 decode/q8_0 < 0.85x at 8K.
hypothesis_seeds.cpu_experiment: Use the RTX box itself (not CPU): clone signalnine/llama-cpp-turboquant-cuda or TheTom/llama-cpp-turboquant, build with GGML_CUDA=ON for sm_75, then `llama-bench -m Qwen3.5-9B-Q4_K_M.gguf -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0` vs `-ctk turbo3 -ctv turbo3` at 512 and 8192 ctx, plus llama-perplexity --chunks 8 for PPL. Compare against the RTX 3090 row in docs/benchmarks.md (0.96x/0.98x).
hypothesis_seeds.est_cost: Local only: ~1-2 h build + ~30-45 min bench; 0 GPU rental $, well within the 3 GPU-h/month budget.

hypothesis_seeds.claim: Sparse V dequant gives a comparable (+15-22%) long-context decode gain on CUDA/Turing as it does on Apple Metal (+22.8% at 32K), because it is an attention-aware optimization independent of the GPU vendor.
hypothesis_seeds.falsifier: Measure turbo3 decode at 32K with sparse V on vs off on the 2070S; claim is false if the delta is < 5%.
hypothesis_seeds.cpu_experiment: On the RTX box: llama-bench or llama-server with TURBO sparse-V enabled vs disabled, -ctk turbo3 -ctv turbo3, pp32768+tg128, Qwen3.5-9B Q4_K_M. Also run the q8_0 control (expected ~+5% if the mechanism is general).

hypothesis_seeds.claim: For the 8 GB VRAM box, q8_0-K + turbo4-V (or turbo3-V) is strictly better than symmetric turbo3: it keeps PPL within ~1-2% of q8_0 while still cutting KV memory ~25-50%, and it avoids the symmetric-turbo catastrophic failure on Q4_K_M weights.
hypothesis_seeds.falsifier: Run llama-perplexity on Qwen3.5-9B Q4_K_M for q8_0/q8_0, q8_0/turbo4, q8_0/turbo3, turbo3/turbo3; claim is false if symmetric turbo3 stays within 2% PPL of q8_0 OR if q8_0/turbo4 exceeds +3%.
hypothesis_seeds.cpu_experiment: Perplexity-only runs on the 2070S (GPU) at 512 ctx, 8 and 32 chunks, wikitext-2; plus a memory check (`llama-server` KV MiB at 32K for each config) to quantify the 8 GB win.

hypothesis_seeds.claim: A tiny (<=2B) draft model sharing the same turbo3 KV cache can recover most of the 0.72-0.88x decode gap on the 2070S via speculative decoding, because the bottleneck is per-position dequant in the target, which the draft amortises.
hypothesis_seeds.falsifier: Implement/serve speculative decoding with a 0.5-2B draft and measure tokens/s vs plain turbo3 decode at 8K; claim is false if the accepted-token rate does not raise net decode above 1.0x q8_0.
hypothesis_seeds.cpu_experiment: Start on CPU with llama.cpp `--model-draft` on the 4-core ARM box at small ctx to validate acceptance rates, then confirm on the 2070S. Measure accepted tokens/step and net tok/s.
hypothesis_seeds.est_cost: CPU validation is local and free; GPU confirmation <1 GPU-h.

hypothesis_seeds.claim: The block-32 + graph-side-WHT + pre-rotate-queries design is vendor-portable and, on the ARM CPU box, turbo3 KV decode is not slower than q8_0 in tokens/s (dequant is pure ALU: centroid lookup + multiply vs int8*scale), so a tiny model on CPU can use 4.6x-smaller KV for the same speed.
hypothesis_seeds.falsifier: Build llama.cpp CPU (no GPU) on the 4-core ARM box and llama-bench -ctk turbo3 -ctv turbo3 vs q8_0 at 2K/4K; claim is false if turbo3 decode < 0.85x q8_0.
hypothesis_seeds.cpu_experiment: CPU-only llama-bench on the ARM box with a <=2B gguf (Qwen3.5-2B) at 2048/4096 ctx; report tokens/s and, if available, tokens/J. Also record peak RSS to confirm the KV saving is real on ordinary RAM.

hypothesis_seeds.claim: Because llama.cpp upstream has now merged Hadamard KV rotation with CUDA kernels (PRs #21038/#23615 per main README), the 2070S can get turbo4-class rotated q4_0 KV without the TurboQuant fork, reaching q8_0-competitive decode.
hypothesis_seeds.falsifier: Build upstream llama.cpp with GGML_CUDA on the 2070S and measure `-ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0` with rotation on vs off; claim is false if rotated q4_0 decode is not within 10% of q8_0 or if PPL degrades >2%.
hypothesis_seeds.cpu_experiment: Not CPU: on the 2070S, compare stock q4_0 KV with the merged Hadamard-rotation path against q8_0 and against the fork's turbo4, same model/ctx.

open_questions: What exactly is 'decode-speed parity' scoped to? In this branch it means turbo3 decode matching q8_0 decode tok/s; it is explicitly not fp16 parity and not prefill parity (prefill is already 0.99-1.02x). Confirm no other definition was intended.

The branch tip contains two unreconciled prefill stories - 'optimized dequant' (block-128, flat 0.98x, README 2524 tok/s) vs 'block-32 + graph WHT' (2747 tok/s, 1.02x). Which one is the shipped configuration on current main?

Does the signalnine CUDA fork / TheTom/llama-cpp-turboquant build for Turing sm_75 (compute capability 7.5), and does the 2070S's smaller L2 (4 MB vs 3090's 6 MB) reproduce the M1-style constant-cache cliff for turbo3?
No measurement anywhere in this clone uses an RTX 2070 SUPER or any 8 GB consumer card; the closest is RTX 3090 (24 GB, Ampere). How much of the 3090's 0.96x/0.98x transfers to Turing?

The decode-speed-parity branch's mid-branch docs contradict its terminal commit about whether the fp16 LUT should be merged; which individual claims (if any) should be treated as superseded?
